title: Readiness diagnostic and routing
outcome: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.

title: Equation and inequality repair
outcome: Classify and solve common equation and inequality families while distinguishing reversible steps from candidate-generating steps.

title: Factoring and polynomial structure repair
outcome: Recognize and apply the principal factoring structures needed for polynomial-function analysis.

title: Rational expressions and restrictions repair
outcome: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.

title: Radicals and rational exponents repair
outcome: Move among radical and rational-exponent forms, simplify exact values, and reject extraneous candidates.

title: Exponential and logarithmic algebra repair
outcome: Apply exponent and logarithm laws, convert between inverse forms, and solve basic equations with valid domains.

title: Function notation and graph reading repair
outcome: Evaluate functions, solve output conditions, and read domain, range, intercepts, extrema, and intervals from graphs.

title: Mixed readiness synthesis
outcome: Select methods across prerequisite strands, justify restrictions, and communicate exact and approximate results.

title: Quantities, variables, and dependency
outcome: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

title: Relations and functions
outcome: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

title: Function notation, evaluation, and solving
outcome: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

title: Words, tables, graphs, and formulas
outcome: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

title: Domain from formulas
outcome: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

title: Domain from context
outcome: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

title: Range and global graph behavior
outcome: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

title: Piecewise-defined functions
outcome: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

title: Average rate of change
outcome: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

title: Function representation and modeling studio
outcome: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

title: Parent-function atlas
outcome: Recognize benchmark function families by domain, range, symmetry, intercepts, end behavior, and rate patterns.

title: Coordinate mappings and transformation logic
outcome: Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.

title: Vertical translations
outcome: Analyze how adding a constant outside a function changes outputs, range, intercepts, extrema, and asymptotes.

title: Horizontal translations
outcome: Analyze how replacing x by x-h changes input locations, domain, intercepts, extrema, and vertical asymptotes.

title: Reflections and symmetry
outcome: Reflect function graphs across coordinate axes and connect reflection rules with even and odd symmetry.

title: Vertical and horizontal scaling
outcome: Distinguish output scaling from input scaling and determine the resulting stretches, compressions, domains, and ranges.

title: Combined transformations
outcome: Analyze and graph functions with several transformations by tracking inputs, outputs, and key features.

title: Sums and differences of functions
outcome: Add and subtract functions pointwise, determine the common domain, and interpret combined outputs.

title: Products and quotients of functions
outcome: Multiply and divide functions pointwise while analyzing zeros, restrictions, and combined graph behavior.

title: Reconstructing formulas from transformed graphs
outcome: Use parent-family features, transformations, and one or more data points to construct and verify a function formula.

title: Composition as sequential processing
outcome: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

title: Composition from formulas
outcome: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

title: Composition from tables and graphs
outcome: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

title: Domains of composite functions
outcome: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

title: One-to-one functions
outcome: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

title: Constructing inverse functions
outcome: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

title: Graphs and verification of inverses
outcome: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

title: Domain restrictions and radical inverses
outcome: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

title: Model construction and validation
outcome: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

title: Power functions and dominant behavior
outcome: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

title: Polynomial functions, degree, and leading term
outcome: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

title: End behavior
outcome: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

title: Zeros, factors, and intercepts
outcome: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

title: Multiplicity and sign behavior
outcome: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

title: Graph construction from structure
outcome: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

title: Turning points and local versus global behavior
outcome: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

title: Intermediate Value reasoning and root bounds
outcome: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

title: Polynomial division
outcome: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

title: Remainder and factor theorems
outcome: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

title: Rational-root candidates and root search
outcome: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

title: Complex zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
outcome: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

title: Building polynomial models and finding numerical roots
outcome: Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.

title: Rational functions and their domains
outcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

title: Equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes
outcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

title: Vertical asymptotes and local behavior
outcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

title: Horizontal asymptotes and end behavior
outcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

title: Slant and polynomial asymptotes
outcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

title: Intercepts and sign charts
outcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

title: Complete rational graph construction
outcome: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

title: Rational equations and function intersections
outcome: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

title: Rational inequalities
outcome: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

title: Variation and rational models
outcome: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

title: Partial-fraction structure
outcome: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

title: Additive versus multiplicative change
outcome: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.

title: Exponential functions and parameters
outcome: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.

title: Exponential transformations
outcome: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.

title: Growth and decay models
outcome: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.

title: Compound interest and effective rate
outcome: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.

title: Continuous growth and the number e
outcome: Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.

title: Exponential regression and residuals
outcome: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.

title: Logistic and bounded growth
outcome: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.

title: Logarithms as inverse functions
outcome: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.

title: Logarithmic graphs and transformations
outcome: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.

title: Logarithm laws
outcome: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.

title: Solving exponential equations
outcome: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.

title: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
outcome: Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.

title: Systems as intersections and models
outcome: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

title: Nonlinear systems
outcome: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

title: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
outcome: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

title: Systems in three variables
outcome: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

title: Matrix notation and operations
outcome: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

title: Augmented matrices and row operations
outcome: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

title: Gaussian elimination and echelon form
outcome: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

title: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
outcome: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

title: Determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices
outcome: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

title: Linear transformations and multivariable modeling
outcome: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.
